'''''Acacia provincialis''''', commonly known as '''swamp wattle'''<ref name=ssa/> or '''wirilda'''<ref name=vic>{{cite web|url=https://vicflora.rbg.vic.gov.au/flora/taxon/70059a9d-a1fc-46b1-8339-0034360edf0c|title=''Acacia provincialis'' A.Camus Wirilda|access-date=1 June 2019|work=VicFlora|publisher=Royal Botanic Gardens Foundation Victoria}}</ref> or '''water wattle''' or '''perennial wattle''',<ref name=lucid/> is a tree or shrub belonging to the genus ''[[Acacia]]'' and the subgenus ''Phyllodineae'' native to southern and south eastern [[Australia]].

==Description==
The tree has a slender and erect habit and typically grows to a height of up to {{convert|10|m|ft|1}}. It has a bushy crown and usually has a single stem but can divide into several stems at ground level<ref name=ssa/> which have smooth grey coloured bark. The branchlets are usually pendulous and are angled or flattened and a reddish-brown often covered with a white powdery finish.<ref name=vic/> It has straight or shallowly recurved, [[Glabrousness (botany)|glabrous]], blue-green to grey-green [[phyllode]]s<ref name=ssa/> that have a narrowly [[oblanceolate]] to narrowly elliptic or linear shape with a length of {{cvt|7|to|22|cm}} and a width of {{cvt|3|to|15|mm}}. It blooms throughout the year<ref name=lucid/> but most heavily between September and January producing [[racemose]] [[inflorescence]]s with spherical flower-heads containing between 18 and 50 flowered golden to pale yellow coloured flowers. After flowering linear brown [[seed pod]]s form that are up {{cvt|16|cm}} in length and {{cvt|5|to|17|mm}} wide with a firm papery texture. The dull to slightly shiny dark brown to black seeds within the pods have an oblong to oblong-elliptic shape and a length of {{cvt|4|to|6|mm}}.<ref name=vic/>

==Distribution==
It is [[endemism|endemic]] to [[Kangaroo Island]], the [[Fleurieu Peninsula]] and the [[Mount Lofty Ranges]] of [[South Australia]] and is also present much of eastern and central of [[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]] where it is found in damp areas in and along the margins of swamp and creeks growing in sandy, clay or loamy soils.<ref name=ssa>{{cite web|url=https://spapps.environment.sa.gov.au/SeedsOfSA/speciesinformation.html?rid=204|title=''Acacia provincialis''(Leguminosae) Swamp Wattle|access-date=31 May 2019|work=Seeds of South Australia|publisher=[[Government of South Australia]]}}</ref> In Victoria the bulk of the population is found between the [[Glenelg River (Victoria)|Glenelg River]] in the [[Grampians National Park|Grampian Ranges]]<ref name=lucid>{{cite web|url=https://apps.lucidcentral.org/wattle/text/entities/acacia_provincialis.htm|title=Acacia provincialis|author=A.Camus|access-date=1 June 2019|work=Wattle - Acacias of Australia|publisher=[[Department of the Environment and Energy]]}}</ref> to near [[Melbourne]] where it is often a part of open-forest communities in poorly drained soils located well inland from the coast.<ref name=vic/> Specimens have also been collected from [[Tasmania]] from [[King Island (Tasmania)|King Island]] and near [[Launceston, Tasmania|Launceston]].<ref name=lucid/>
